outcome: Controllers can make reproducible probabilistic decisions with simulator-owned stochastic distributions
owner_impact: Controller code can use rng.uniform(a, b), rng.bernoulli(p), and rng.normal(mean, stddev). Every agent receives its own deterministic stream derived from the Experiment run seed, so one agent's random draws cannot perturb another agent's sequence. Reset/replay reconstructs the exact streams. Raw RNG state, reseeding, and host-language randomness remain unavailable.

technical_evidence: Capability controller.stochastic_distributions owns the three Controller surfaces rng.uniform, rng.bernoulli and rng.normal under vlab.controller-stochasticity/1.
Browser and MCP controller compilers remain byte-identical and lower dotted stochastic calls into the existing typed vlab.controller-ir/0.1 call representation.
Rust/WASM executes stochastic calls from one vlab.rng/splitmix64-domain/1 controller stream per stable agent index, derived from the run SEED.
Reset recreates every per-agent controller stream; draw-count independence across agents and seed sensitivity are covered by Rust runtime regressions.
The capability protocol publishes distribution semantics, draw counts, RNG contract version and per-agent stream scope while raw stream access and reseeding remain forbidden.
